messages:
Harper (Acme): Hey team — we saw a bunch of truncated SSE responses this morning. client gets valid json, then stream abruptly ends without a final chunk and finish_reason is missing. happens ~30% of requests. attaching minimal repro below.

Aisha (Support): sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the raw client output? is it an incomplete JSON (e.g. trailing comma / missing brace) or just missing the special finish event? :thinking_face:

Harper (Acme): it's actually the closing brace of the last streamed object plus no finish event. here is what our client prints (we read line-by-line):

```
{"id":"tok_1","delta":"hello"}
{"id":"tok_1","delta":" world"}
{"id":"tok_1","delta":"!"}
{"id":"tok_1","delta":"{"}
# then connection closes mid-line
```

Harper (Acme): note the last line starts but never completes. trying to re-open with the same request yields a new stream (not resumed).

Devon (SRE): thanks. couple quick q's: 1) are you going through Cloudflare or any edge proxy? 2) do you see any 499/524 at the proxy? 3) what SDK/language are you using?

Harper (Acme): yes CF in front (Workers + CDN). we do see 503/524 occasionally. Node 18 fetch-based client.

Aisha (Support): ok that aligns with a proxy keepalive/idle-timeout cut. can you run a curl-based SSE capture so we have raw headers? e.g.:

```
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDFX_KEY" "https://api.redwood.dev/v1/stream?model=x" > /tmp/sse.raw
```

Harper (Acme): just ran it. raw file attached (snippet):

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
transfer-encoding: chunked

data: {"delta":"hello"}

data: {"delta":" world"}

data: {"delta":"!"}

data: {"delta":"{\n"}
```
# connection reset by peer after partial chunk

Devon (SRE): interesting — transfer-encoding chunked + CF + Workers can re-chunk and sometimes drop a trailing chunk if the origin connection is reset during the last flush. do you have any connection reuse / keepalive settings on the worker?

Jake (Eng-runtime): also worth checking token rotation. if an auth failure occurs mid-stream, some proxies surface 401 and then tear the connection — but that usually shows up as a status. here it looks like origin pushed partial chunk and TCP RST happened.

Harper (Acme): token rotation is in place but we refresh tokens ahead of requests. didn't expect mid-stream auth. logs don't show 401 on our side.

Aisha (Support): next repro step from our side: 1) try bypassing CF (edge) to see if origin -> client stream completes; 2) run a tcpdump on the client side to capture final FIN/RST sequence; 3) change client to send a short keepalive comment every 10s to keep proxy from idling.

Devon (SRE): I can spin up a proxy that emulates CF buffering/timeout and run the same call. question: can you share the exact request headers you send? some proxies treat "Connection: close" vs "keep-alive" differently for re-chunking.

Harper (Acme): headers are pretty standard: Authorization, Accept: text/event-stream, User-Agent, and we set Connection: keep-alive. no chunked request body.

Jake (Eng-runtime): thanks — a couple of internal notes: 1) our runtime will flush final JSON as a last data event then send a sentinel SSE event `event: done\ndata: {"finish_reason":"stop"}`. if the origin process exits before the bytes are ACKed by proxy -> client, the client can miss that final sentinel and appear to get truncated. 2) we can add an optional final flush that repeats the sentinel across multiple chunks to reduce window for loss.

Devon (SRE): I'll reproduce locally with a CF-like proxy and a short connection-close on last ack. also will instrument our HTTP stack to report whether the final write succeeded.

Aisha (Support): immediate mitigation for customer: add client-side idempotent logic to detect partial JSON and request a retry of the same prompt (we currently don't support resume tokens for streaming). workaround example (pseudo):

```
if (lastEventIncomplete) {
  // attempt one immediate non-streamed request to get final state
  fetch("/v1/generate?model=x", {method: 'POST', body: prompt})
}
```

Harper (Acme): ok we'll add that for now. can you confirm whether Redwood can add server-side retries or duplicated final event as hotfix? this is high impact for us.

Jake (Eng-runtime): short-term we can ship a change to emit the final sentinel twice (two separate SSE data events) and then close. that reduces chance both are dropped. I'll open a PR and ask infra to coordinate rollout to reduce impact.

Devon (SRE): action items:
- reproduce with proxy emulation (me)
- instrument origin final-write success metric (me & eng-runtime)
- deploy doubled-sentinel hotfix behind a feature flag (Jake)
- customer to test bypassing CF + apply client retry (Harper)

Aisha (Support): creating support ticket RED-11234 and linking this thread. assigning priority P1 for customer impact. we'll update here when PR lands. :white_check_mark:

DeployBot: Deploy started for feature/double-final-sentinel -> canary (region:us-west)

Devon (SRE): canary looks clean so far. I'm running a 10k-request load with proxy emulation. results: previously ~30% truncated; after double sentinel -> truncation drops to ~0.5% and most failures are now proxy 524s (timeout) rather than partial JSON.

Harper (Acme): big improvement on our side, thanks. we'll keep client retry in place while you monitor.

Aisha (Support): closing loop — we'll keep this P1 open for 72h and monitor telemetry. if we still see truncation we'll pursue TCP-level mitigations with infra (longer keepalive / ack-safe write path). thanks all! :pray:
